text: The Patriots' dominant 45-17 victory over the Raiders came at a steep cost, with running back TreVeyon Henderson sidelined for multiple weeks due to a high ankle sprain and left tackle Will Campbell diagnosed with an MCL sprain in his right knee that will cost him game action, forcing the team to shuffle its depth chart at two critical positions. Despite operating without his top receiver and both starting cornerbacks, Drake Maye delivered his best performance of the season, accounting for five touchdowns and showcasing the kind of efficiency that suggests he's found both his confidence and his deep ball after a shaky start to the year. The front office moved quickly to bolster the practice squad, signing running back Hassan Haskins and cornerback D'Shawn Jamison while releasing linebacker Jose Ramirez, providing some insurance as injuries continue to mount. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the week's developments in his Monday press conference, with film review of Maye's masterful Raiders performance offering plenty of reasons for optimism despite the mounting injury concerns.
